7.18 SQLite and optional Turso

The OCaml archive tools and probes open their databases through firstpair-tursolite, one interface over SQLite and Turso whose manual, tursolite, is on the First Pair unix shelf. Archives stay in WAL between runs (Keep_wal and Journal::Existing there), and closed archives are read with immutable, which writes nothing beside the file.

SQLite is the ordinary checkpoint backend. Turso support is pinned to embedded 0.8.3 and uses explicit MVCC transactions during work. The filename extension .sqlite3 alone does not identify which engine owns a checkpoint; retain its .engine.json marker. The wrapper can export a closed checkpoint for legacy reading, but an active archive is not a generic file-copy snapshot.

Migration refuses an uncheckpointed SQLite WAL and keeps a before-turso copy. Do not remove ownership markers, edit an active database with another engine, or copy only its main file while the writer has WAL/MVCC state. A retained PID is a liveness guard; inspect a failed owner rather than clearing its state blindly. Ordinary comparison databases are project checkpoints, not Lightroom catalogs.

The Rust turso-probe and OCaml turso_probe_oxcaml.ml/C bindings are experimental smoke tests for typed values and concurrent writers. The OCaml FFI build requires its matching Turso SDK library and is not part of the ordinary build. Do not confuse a probe’s 64 inserted synthetic rows with a photograph comparison or production archive acceptance. make build-turso reports the separate supported build path; read its output before using the experiment.
